newsitem.title: UK: Fannie Mae eyes jumbo French franc Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae eyes jumbo French franc Eurobond.

text.p: Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) may launch a jumbo French franc bond after investor presentations later this month, syndicate managers said on Tuesday.
Merrill Lynch and Societe Generale have arranged meetings for November 18, 19 and 20, an official at SocGen said.
But Fannie Mae had not yet awarded a mandate for a Eurobond, and would only decide whether or not to tap the sector after investor feedback, the official said.
Other Paris-based syndicate managers said a deal for between 3-5 billion French francs was expected.
Maturity would range between 9-12 years, and the launch spread would be between 10-12 basis points over OATs.
"What is known is the rough range Fannie Mae is looking at," said a syndicate manager at a French bank. "Where it materialises depends on what investors want."
Another trader said it was difficult to say whether a Fannie Mae deal would be well-received.
"One scenario is the leads may force it a little to get it done as they are unlikely to want to wait until January," the Eurobond trader said.
"Fannie Mae is a fairly aggressive borrower, and they were shown fairly punchy pricing levels during bidding for the deal," he said.

With French government bond yields at their lowest level since February 1994, dealers said many investors thought the market had peaked and were only buying paper that provided yield pick-up or good value.
"Ten-year OATs are now yielding 5.88 percent, and investors may buy Eurobonds instead in order to get a six percent yield again," a syndicate manager said.
